5653   /**
5654    * Converts a string to PascalCase format.
5655    *
5656    * <p>
5657    * Handles various input formats:
5658    * <ul>
5659    *   <li>Space-separated: "hello world" → "HelloWorld"</li>
5660    *   <li>CamelCase: "helloWorld" → "HelloWorld"</li>
5661    *   <li>Snake_case: "hello_world" → "HelloWorld"</li>
5662    *   <li>Kebab-case: "hello-world" → "HelloWorld"</li>
5663    * </ul>
5664    *
5665    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
5666    * <p class='bjava'>
5667    *    pascalCase(<jk>null</jk>);                    <jc>// null</jc>
5668    *    pascalCase(<js>""</js>);                      <jc>// ""</jc>
5669    *    pascalCase(<js>"hello world"</js>);           <jc>// "HelloWorld"</jc>
5670    *    pascalCase(<js>"helloWorld"</js>);            <jc>// "HelloWorld"</jc>
5671    *    pascalCase(<js>"hello_world"</js>);           <jc>// "HelloWorld"</jc>
5672    *    pascalCase(<js>"hello-world"</js>);           <jc>// "HelloWorld"</jc>
5673    * </p>
5674    *
5675    * @param str The string to convert.
5676    * @return The PascalCase string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
5677    */
5678   public static String pascalCase(String str) {
5679      if (isEmpty(str))
5680         return str;
5681
5682      var words = splitWords(str);
5683      if (words.isEmpty())
5684         return "";
5685
5686      var result = new StringBuilder();
5687      for (var word : words) {
5688         result.append(capitalize(lowerCaseRoot(word)));
5689      }
5690
5691      return result.toString();
5692   }

5694   /**
5695    * Pluralizes a word based on a count.
5696    *
5697    * <p>
5698    * Simple pluralization that adds "s" to most words, with basic rules for words ending in "s", "x", "z", "ch", "sh" (add "es"),
5699    * and words ending in "y" preceded by a consonant (replace "y" with "ies").
5700    *
5701    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
5702    * <p class='bjava'>
5703    *    pluralize(<js>"cat"</js>, <js>1</js>);        <jc>// "cat"</jc>
5704    *    pluralize(<js>"cat"</js>, <js>2</js>);        <jc>// "cats"</jc>
5705    *    pluralize(<js>"box"</js>, <js>2</js>);        <jc>// "boxes"</jc>
5706    *    pluralize(<js>"city"</js>, <js>2</js>);       <jc>// "cities"</jc>
5707    * </p>
5708    *
5709    * @param word The word to pluralize.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returned as-is).
5710    * @param count The count to determine if pluralization is needed.
5711    * @return The pluralized word if count is not 1, otherwise the original word.
5712    */
5713   public static String pluralize(String word, int count) {
5714      if (word == null || word.isEmpty())
5715         return word;
5716      if (count == 1)
5717         return word;
5718
5719      var lower = lowerCaseRoot(word);
5720      var length = word.length();
5721
5722      // Words ending in s, x, z, ch, sh -> add "es"
5723      if (lower.endsWith("s") || lower.endsWith("x") || lower.endsWith("z") || lower.endsWith("ch") || lower.endsWith("sh")) {
5724         return word + "es";
5725      }
5726
5727      // Words ending in "y" preceded by a consonant -> replace "y" with "ies"
5728      if (length > 1 && lower.endsWith("y")) {
5729         var secondLast = lower.charAt(length - 2);
5730         if (! VOWEL.contains(secondLast)) {
5731            return word.substring(0, length - 1) + "ies";
5732         }
5733      }
5734
5735      // Words ending in "f" or "fe" -> replace with "ves" (basic rule)
5736      if (lower.endsWith("f")) {
5737         return word.substring(0, length - 1) + "ves";
5738      }
5739      if (lower.endsWith("fe")) {
5740         return word.substring(0, length - 2) + "ves";
5741      }
5742
5743      // Default: add "s"
5744      return word + "s";
5745   }

5747   /**
5748    * Generated a random UUID with the specified number of characters.
5749    *
5750    * <p>
5751    * Characters are composed of lower-case ASCII letters and numbers only.
5752    *
5753    * <p>
5754    * This method conforms to the restrictions for hostnames as specified in <a class="doclink" href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc952">RFC 952</a>
5755    * Since each character has 36 possible values, the square approximation formula for the number of generated IDs
5756    * that would produce a 50% chance of collision is:
5757    * <c>sqrt(36^N)</c>.
5758    * Dividing this number by 10 gives you an approximation of the number of generated IDs needed to produce a
5759    * &lt;1% chance of collision.
5760    *
5761    * <p>
5762    * For example, given 5 characters, the number of generated IDs need to produce a &lt;1% chance of collision would
5763    * be:
5764    * <c>sqrt(36^5)/10=777</c>
5765    *
5766    * @param numchars The number of characters in the generated UUID.
5767    * @return A new random UUID.
5768    */
5769   public static String random(int numchars) {
5770      var sb = new StringBuilder(numchars);
5771      for (var i = 0; i < numchars; i++) {
5772         var c = RANDOM.nextInt(36) + 97;
5773         if (c > 'z')
5774            c -= ('z' - '0' + 1);
5775         sb.append((char)c);
5776      }
5777      return sb.toString();
5778   }

5780   /**
5781    * Generates a random alphabetic string of the specified length.
5782    *
5783    * <p>
5784    * Characters are composed of upper-case and lower-case ASCII letters (a-z, A-Z).
5785    *
5786    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
5787    * <p class='bjava'>
5788    *    randomAlphabetic(<jk>5</jk>);  <jc>// "aBcDe"</jc>
5789    * </p>
5790    *
5791    * @param length The length of the generated string.
5792    * @return A new random alphabetic string.
5793    */
5794   public static String randomAlphabetic(int length) {
5795      if (length < 0)
5796         throw iaex("Length must be non-negative: " + length);
5797      var sb = new StringBuilder(length);
5798      for (var i = 0; i < length; i++) {
5799         var c = RANDOM.nextInt(52);
5800         if (c < 26)
5801            sb.append((char)('a' + c));
5802         else
5803            sb.append((char)('A' + c - 26));
5804      }
5805      return sb.toString();
5806   }

5808   /**
5809    * Generates a random alphanumeric string of the specified length.
5810    *
5811    * <p>
5812    * Characters are composed of upper-case and lower-case ASCII letters and digits (a-z, A-Z, 0-9).
5813    *
5814    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
5815    * <p class='bjava'>
5816    *    randomAlphanumeric(<jk>8</jk>);  <jc>// "aB3dE5fG"</jc>
5817    * </p>
5818    *
5819    * @param length The length of the generated string.
5820    * @return A new random alphanumeric string.
5821    */
5822   public static String randomAlphanumeric(int length) {
5823      if (length < 0)
5824         throw iaex("Length must be non-negative: " + length);
5825      var sb = new StringBuilder(length);
5826      for (var i = 0; i < length; i++) {
5827         var c = RANDOM.nextInt(62);
5828         if (c < 10)
5829            sb.append((char)('0' + c));
5830         else if (c < 36)
5831            sb.append((char)('a' + c - 10));
5832         else
5833            sb.append((char)('A' + c - 36));
5834      }
5835      return sb.toString();
5836   }

5838   /**
5839    * Generates a random ASCII string of the specified length.

5841    * <p>
5842    * Characters are composed of printable ASCII characters (32-126).
5843    *
5844    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
5845    * <p class='bjava'>
5846    *    randomAscii(<jk>10</jk>);  <jc>// "!@#$%^&amp;*()"</jc>
5847    * </p>
5848    *
5849    * @param length The length of the generated string.
5850    * @return A new random ASCII string.
5851    */
5852   public static String randomAscii(int length) {
5853      if (length < 0)
5854         throw iaex("Length must be non-negative: " + length);
5855      var sb = new StringBuilder(length);
5856      for (var i = 0; i < length; i++) {
5857         sb.append((char)(32 + RANDOM.nextInt(95))); // 95 printable ASCII chars (32-126)
5858      }
5859      return sb.toString();
5860   }

5901    */
5902   public static String randomString(int length, String chars) {
5903      if (length < 0)
5904         throw iaex("Length must be non-negative: " + length);

5907      var sb = new StringBuilder(length);

5915   /**
5916    * Calculates a simple readability score for a string.
5917    *
5918    * <p>
5919    * Uses a simplified Flesch Reading Ease-like formula based on:
5920    * <ul>
5921    *   <li>Average words per sentence</li>
5922    *   <li>Average syllables per word (estimated)</li>
5923    * </ul>
5924    * Returns a score from 0-100, where higher scores indicate easier reading.
5925    *
5926    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
5927    * <p class='bjava'>
5928    *    readabilityScore(<js>"The cat sat."</js>);      <jc>// Higher score (simple)</jc>
5929    *    readabilityScore(<js>"The sophisticated..."</js>); <jc>// Lower score (complex)</jc>
5930    * </p>
5931    *
5932    * @param str The string to analyze. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
5933    * @return A readability score from 0-100, or <c>0.0</c> if the string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
5934    */
5935   public static double readabilityScore(String str) {
5936      if (isEmpty(str))
5937         return 0.0;
5938
5939      var words = extractWords(str);
5940      if (words.isEmpty())
5941         return 0.0;
5942
5943      // Count sentences (ending with . ! ?)
5944      var sentenceCount = 0;
5945      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
5946         var c = str.charAt(i);
5947         if (c == '.' || c == '!' || c == '?') {
5948            sentenceCount++;
5949         }
5950      }
5951      if (sentenceCount == 0)
5952         sentenceCount = 1; // At least one sentence
5953
5954      // Calculate average words per sentence
5955      var avgWordsPerSentence = (double)words.size() / sentenceCount;
5956
5957      // Estimate average syllables per word (simplified: count vowel groups)
5958      var totalSyllables = 0;
5959      for (var word : words) {
5960         totalSyllables += estimateSyllables(word);
5961      }
5962      var avgSyllablesPerWord = (double)totalSyllables / words.size();
5963
5964      // Simplified Flesch Reading Ease formula
5965      // Score = 206.835 - (1.015 * ASL) - (84.6 * ASW)
5966      // Where ASL = average sentence length (words), ASW = average syllables per word
5967      var score = 206.835 - (1.015 * avgWordsPerSentence) - (84.6 * avgSyllablesPerWord);
5968
5969      // Clamp to 0-100 range
5970      return Math.max(0.0, Math.min(100.0, score));
5971   }

5973   /**
5974    * Converts an arbitrary object to a readable string format suitable for debugging and testing.
5975    *
5976    * <p>This method provides intelligent formatting for various Java types, recursively processing
5977    * nested structures to create human-readable representations. It's extensively used throughout
5978    * the Juneau framework for test assertions and debugging output.</p>
5979    *
5980    * <h4 class='section'>Type-Specific Formatting:</h4>
5981    * <ul>
5982    *    <li><b>null:</b> Returns <js>null</js></li>
5983    *    <li><b>Optional:</b> Recursively formats the contained value (or <js>null</js> if empty)</li>
5984    *    <li><b>Collections:</b> Formats as <js>"[item1,item2,item3]"</js> with comma-separated elements</li>
5985    *    <li><b>Maps:</b> Formats as <js>"{key1=value1,key2=value2}"</js> with comma-separated entries</li>
5986    *    <li><b>Map.Entry:</b> Formats as <js>"key=value"</js></li>
5987    *    <li><b>Arrays:</b> Converts to list format <js>"[item1,item2,item3]"</js></li>
5988    *    <li><b>Iterables/Iterators/Enumerations:</b> Converts to list and formats recursively</li>
5989    *    <li><b>GregorianCalendar:</b> Formats as ISO instant timestamp</li>
5990    *    <li><b>Date:</b> Formats as ISO instant string (e.g., <js>"2023-12-25T10:30:00Z"</js>)</li>
5991    *    <li><b>InputStream:</b> Converts to hexadecimal representation</li>
5992    *    <li><b>Reader:</b> Reads content and returns as string</li>
5993    *    <li><b>File:</b> Reads file content and returns as string</li>
5994    *    <li><b>byte[]:</b> Converts to hexadecimal representation</li>
5995    *    <li><b>Enum:</b> Returns the enum name via {@link Enum#name()}</li>
5996    *    <li><b>All other types:</b> Uses {@link Object#toString()}</li>
5997    * </ul>
5998    *
5999    * <h4 class='section'>Examples:</h4>
6000    * <p class='bjava'>
6001    *    <jc>// Collections</jc>
6002    *    readable(List.of("a", "b", "c")) <jc>// Returns: "[a,b,c]"</jc>
6003    *    readable(Set.of(1, 2, 3)) <jc>// Returns: "[1,2,3]" (order may vary)</jc>
6004    *
6005    *    <jc>// Maps</jc>
6006    *    readable(Map.of("foo", "bar", "baz", 123)) <jc>// Returns: "{foo=bar,baz=123}"</jc>
6007    *
6008    *    <jc>// Arrays</jc>
6009    *    readable(ints(1, 2, 3)) <jc>// Returns: "[1,2,3]"</jc>
6010    *    readable(new String[]{"a", "b"}) <jc>// Returns: "[a,b]"</jc>
6011    *
6012    *    <jc>// Nested structures</jc>
6013    *    readable(List.of(Map.of("x", 1), Set.of("a", "b"))) <jc>// Returns: "[{x=1},[a,b]]"</jc>
6014    *
6015    *    <jc>// Special types</jc>
6016    *    readable(Optional.of("test")) <jc>// Returns: "test"</jc>
6017    *    readable(Optional.empty()) <jc>// Returns: null</jc>
6018    *    readable(new Date(1640995200000L)) <jc>// Returns: "2022-01-01T00:00:00Z"</jc>
6019    *    readable(MyEnum.FOO) <jc>// Returns: "FOO"</jc>
6020    * </p>
6021    *
6022    * <h4 class='section'>Recursive Processing:</h4>
6023    * <p>The method recursively processes nested structures, so complex objects containing
6024    * collections, maps, and arrays are fully flattened into readable format. This makes it
6025    * ideal for test assertions where you need to compare complex object structures.</p>
6026    *
6027    * <h4 class='section'>Error Handling:</h4>
6028    * <p>IO operations (reading files, streams) are wrapped in safe() calls, converting
6029    * any exceptions to RuntimeExceptions. Binary data (InputStreams, byte arrays) is
6030    * converted to hexadecimal representation for readability.</p>
6031    *
6032    * @param o The object to convert to readable format. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6033    * @return A readable string representation of the object, or <jk>null</jk> if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
6034    */
6035   public static String readable(Object o) {
6036      if (o == null)
6037         return null;
6038      var c = o.getClass();
6039
6040      // Special case for byte[] - must be handled before general array check
6041      if (c == byte[].class) {
6042         return toHex((byte[])o);
6043      }
6044
6045      // Check cache first
6046      var f = READIFIER_CACHE.get(c, () -> {
6047         // Find readifier from READIFIERS list
6048         // First try exact match, then isAssignableFrom
6049         var readifier = READIFIERS.stream()
6050            .filter(r -> r.forClass() == c || r.forClass().isAssignableFrom(c))
6051            .map(Readifier::toFunction)
6052            .findFirst()
6053            .orElse(null);
6054
6055         // If readifier found, use it
6056         if (readifier != null)
6057            return readifier;
6058
6059         // If no readifier found, check if it's an array
6060         if (c.isArray()) {
6061            return x -> {
6062               var l = list();
6063               for (var i = 0; i < Array.getLength(x); i++) {
6064                  l.add(Array.get(x, i));
6065               }
6066               return readable(l);
6067            };
6068         }
6069
6070         // If no readifier found, use toString() as fallback
6071         return Object::toString;
6072      });
6073
6074      return f.apply(o);
6075   }

6098   /**
6099    * Removes diacritical marks (accents) from characters in a string.
6100    *
6101    * <p>
6102    * Normalizes the string to NFD form and removes combining diacritical marks.
6103    *
6104    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
6105    * <p class='bjava'>
6106    *    removeAccents(<js>"café"</js>);     <jc>// "cafe"</jc>
6107    *    removeAccents(<js>"naïve"</js>);    <jc>// "naive"</jc>
6108    *    removeAccents(<js>"résumé"</js>);   <jc>// "resume"</jc>
6109    * </p>
6110    *
6111    * @param str The string to remove accents from. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6112    * @return The string with accents removed, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6113    */
6114   public static String removeAccents(String str) {
6115      if (str == null)
6116         return null;
6117
6118      // Normalize to NFD (decomposed form)
6119      var normalized = Normalizer.normalize(str, Normalizer.Form.NFD);
6120
6121      // Remove combining diacritical marks (Unicode category Mn)
6122      var sb = new StringBuilder(normalized.length());
6123      for (var i = 0; i < normalized.length(); i++) {
6124         var c = normalized.charAt(i);
6125         var type = Character.getType(c);
6126         // Mn = Nonspacing_Mark (combining marks)
6127         if (type != Character.NON_SPACING_MARK) {
6128            sb.append(c);
6129         }
6130      }
6131
6132      return sb.toString();
6133   }

6147    */
6148   public static String removeAll(String str, String...remove) {
6149      if (str == null)

6154      for (var r : remove) {

6156            result = result.replace(r, "");
6157      }
6158      return result;

6162    * Removes control characters from a string, replacing them with spaces.

6165    * <p class='bjava'>
6166    *    removeControlChars(<js>"hello\u0000\u0001world"</js>);   <jc>// "hello  world"</jc>

6168    * </p>

6171    * @return The string with control characters replaced by spaces (except whitespace control chars), or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6172    */
6173   public static String removeControlChars(String str) {
6174      if (str == null)
6175         return null;
6176      var sb = new StringBuilder();
6177      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
6178         var c = str.charAt(i);
6179         if (Character.isISOControl(c) && ! Character.isWhitespace(c))
6180            sb.append(' ');
6181         else
6182            sb.append(c);
6183      }
6184      return sb.toString();
6185   }

6250   /**

6255    * (e.g., <js>"1_000_000"</js> becomes <js>"1000000"</js>), as Java allows underscores in numeric literals
6256    * but some parsing methods do not support them.

6265    *    removeUnderscores(<js>"hello_world"</js>);      <jc>// "helloworld"</jc>
6266    *    removeUnderscores(<js>"no_underscores"</js>);   <jc>// "nounderscores"</jc>
6267    *    removeUnderscores(<js>"Hello"</js>);            <jc>// "Hello" (no change, same object returned)</jc>
6268    * </p>
6269    *
6270    * @param value The string from which to remove underscores. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.

6275    * @see #parseFloat(String)
6276    * @see #parseNumber(String, Class)
6277    */
6278   public static String removeUnderscores(String value) {
6279      reqnn("value", value);
6280      return notContains(value, '_') ? value : value.replace("_", "");

6283   /**
6284    * Creates a repeated pattern.

6288    * @return A new string consisting of the repeated pattern.
6289    */
6290   public static String repeat(int count, String pattern) {
6291      var sb = new StringBuilder(pattern.length() * count);
6292      for (var i = 0; i < count; i++)
6293         sb.append(pattern);
6294      return sb.toString();

6297   /**
6298    * Replaces <js>"\\uXXXX"</js> character sequences with their unicode characters.
6299    *
6300    * @param s The string to replace unicode sequences in.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
6301    * @return A string with unicode sequences replaced.
6302    */
6303   public static String replaceUnicodeSequences(String s) {
6304
6305      if (s.indexOf('\\') == -1)
6306         return s;
6307
6308      var p = Pattern.compile("\\\\u(\\p{XDigit}{4})");
6309      var m = p.matcher(s);
6310      var sb = new StringBuffer(s.length());
6311
6312      while (m.find()) {
6313         var ch = String.valueOf((char)Integer.parseInt(m.group(1), 16));
6314         m.appendReplacement(sb, Matcher.quoteReplacement(ch));
6315      }
6316
6317      m.appendTail(sb);
6318      return sb.toString();
6319   }

6345    *    right(<jk>null</jk>, 3);          <jc>// null</jc>
6346    *    right(<js>""</js>, 3);            <jc>// ""</jc>
6347    *    right(<js>"hello"</js>, 3);       <jc>// "llo"</jc>
6348    *    right(<js>"hello"</js>, 10);      <jc>// "hello"</jc>
6349    * </p>
6350    *
6351    * @param str The string to get characters from.
6352    * @param len The number of characters to get.
6353    * @return The rightmost characters, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6354    */
6355   public static String right(String str, int len) {
6356      if (str == null)
6357         return null;
6358      if (len < 0)
6359         return "";
6360      if (len >= str.length())
6361         return str;
6362      return str.substring(str.length() - len);
6363   }

6365   /**
6366    * Basic HTML/XML sanitization - removes or escapes potentially dangerous content.
6367    *
6368    * <p>
6369    * Removes HTML/XML tags and escapes special characters so the text renders as plain text.
6370    * This is a basic sanitization - for production use, consider a more robust library.
6371    *
6372    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
6373    * <p class='bjava'>
6374    *    sanitize(<js>"&lt;script&gt;alert('x')&lt;/script&gt;"</js>);     <jc>// "&amp;lt;script&amp;gt;alert('x')&amp;lt;/script&amp;gt;"</jc>
6375    *    sanitize(<js>"Hello &lt;b&gt;World&lt;/b&gt;"</js>);                <jc>// "Hello &amp;lt;b&amp;gt;World&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt;"</jc>
6376    * </p>
6377    *
6378    * @param str The string to sanitize.
6379    * @return The sanitized string with HTML/XML tags escaped, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6380    */
6381   public static String sanitize(String str) {
6382      if (str == null)
6383         return null;
6384      // Escape HTML/XML special characters
6385      return escapeHtml(str);
6386   }

6388   /**
6389    * Calculates the similarity percentage between two strings using Levenshtein distance.
6390    *
6391    * <p>
6392    * Returns a value between 0.0 (completely different) and 1.0 (identical).
6393    *
6394    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
6395    * <p class='bjava'>
6396    *    similarity(<js>"hello"</js>, <js>"hello"</js>);           <jc>// 1.0 (100%)</jc>
6397    *    similarity(<js>"kitten"</js>, <js>"sitting"</js>);        <jc>// ~0.57 (57%)</jc>
6398    *    similarity(<js>"abc"</js>, <js>"xyz"</js>);               <jc>// 0.0 (0%)</jc>
6399    * </p>
6400    *
6401    * @param str1 The first string.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as empty).
6402    * @param str2 The second string.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as empty).
6403    * @return A similarity value between 0.0 and 1.0, where 1.0 means identical.
6404    */
6405   public static double similarity(String str1, String str2) {
6406      if (str1 == null)
6407         str1 = "";
6408      if (str2 == null)
6409         str2 = "";
6410
6411      if (eq(str1, str2))
6412         return 1.0;
6413
6414      var maxLen = Math.max(str1.length(), str2.length());
6415
6416      var distance = levenshteinDistance(str1, str2);
6417      return 1.0 - ((double)distance / maxLen);
6418   }

6420   /**
6421    * Converts a string to snake_case format.
6422    *
6423    * <p>
6424    * Handles various input formats:
6425    * <ul>
6426    *   <li>Space-separated: "hello world" → "hello_world"</li>
6427    *   <li>CamelCase: "helloWorld" → "hello_world"</li>
6428    *   <li>PascalCase: "HelloWorld" → "hello_world"</li>
6429    *   <li>Kebab-case: "hello-world" → "hello_world"</li>
6430    * </ul>
6431    *
6432    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
6433    * <p class='bjava'>
6434    *    snakeCase(<jk>null</jk>);                    <jc>// null</jc>
6435    *    snakeCase(<js>""</js>);                      <jc>// ""</jc>
6436    *    snakeCase(<js>"hello world"</js>);           <jc>// "hello_world"</jc>
6437    *    snakeCase(<js>"helloWorld"</js>);            <jc>// "hello_world"</jc>
6438    *    snakeCase(<js>"HelloWorld"</js>);            <jc>// "hello_world"</jc>
6439    *    snakeCase(<js>"hello-world"</js>);           <jc>// "hello_world"</jc>
6440    * </p>
6441    *
6442    * @param str The string to convert.
6443    * @return The snake_case string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6444    */
6445   public static String snakeCase(String str) {
6446      if (str == null)
6447         return null;
6448      if (isEmpty(str))
6449         return str;
6450
6451      var words = splitWords(str);
6452      if (words.isEmpty())
6453         return "";
6454
6455      var result = new StringBuilder();
6456      for (var i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
6457         if (i > 0)
6458            result.append('_');
6459         result.append(lowerCaseRoot(words.get(i)));
6460      }
6461
6462      return result.toString();
6463   }

6465   /**
6466    * Sorts a string array in natural order.
6467    *
6468    * <p>
6469    * Returns <jk>null</jk> if the array is <jk>null</jk>.
6470    * This method creates a copy of the array and sorts it, leaving the original array unchanged.
6471    *
6472    * <h4 class='section'>Examples:</h4>
6473    * <p class='bjava'>
6474    *    String[] <jv>array</jv> = {<js>"zebra"</js>, <js>"apple"</js>, <js>"banana"</js>};
6475    *    String[] <jv>sorted</jv> = sort(<jv>array</jv>);
6476    *    <jc>// Returns: ["apple", "banana", "zebra"]</jc>
6477    * </p>
6478    *
6479    * @param array The array to sort. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6480    * @return A new sorted array, or an empty array if the array was <jk>null</jk>.
6481    */
6482   public static String[] sort(String[] array) {
6483      if (array == null)
6484         return new String[0];
6485      var result = Arrays.copyOf(array, array.length);
6486      Arrays.sort(result);
6487      return result;
6488   }

6490   /**
6491    * Sorts a string array in case-insensitive order.
6492    *
6493    * <p>
6494    * Returns <jk>null</jk> if the array is <jk>null</jk>.
6495    * This method creates a copy of the array and sorts it using case-insensitive comparison,
6496    * leaving the original array unchanged.
6497    *
6498    * <h4 class='section'>Examples:</h4>
6499    * <p class='bjava'>
6500    *    String[] <jv>array</jv> = {<js>"Zebra"</js>, <js>"apple"</js>, <js>"Banana"</js>};
6501    *    String[] <jv>sorted</jv> = sortIgnoreCase(<jv>array</jv>);
6502    *    <jc>// Returns: ["apple", "Banana", "Zebra"]</jc>
6503    * </p>
6504    *
6505    * @param array The array to sort. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6506    * @return A new sorted array (case-insensitive), or an empty array if the array was <jk>null</jk>.
6507    */
6508   public static String[] sortIgnoreCase(String[] array) {
6509      if (array == null)
6510         return new String[0];
6511      var result = Arrays.copyOf(array, array.length);
6512      Arrays.sort(result, String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER);
6513      return result;
6514   }

6516   /**
6517    * Generates a Soundex code for a string.
6518    *
6519    * <p>
6520    * Soundex is a phonetic algorithm for indexing names by sound. The code consists of
6521    * a letter followed by three digits. Similar-sounding names produce the same code.
6522    *
6523    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
6524    * <p class='bjava'>
6525    *    soundex(<js>"Smith"</js>);   <jc>// "S530"</jc>
6526    *    soundex(<js>"Smythe"</js>);  <jc>// "S530"</jc>
6527    *    soundex(<js>"Robert"</js>);  <jc>// "R163"</jc>
6528    * </p>
6529    *
6530    * @param str The string to generate a Soundex code for. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6531    * @return The Soundex code (1 letter + 3 digits), or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
6532    */
6533   public static String soundex(String str) {
6534      if (isEmpty(str))
6535         return null;
6536
6537      var upper = str.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
6538      var result = new StringBuilder(4);
6539      result.append(upper.charAt(0));
6540
6541      // Soundex mapping: 0 = AEIOUHWY, 1 = BFPV, 2 = CGJKQSXZ, 3 = DT, 4 = L, 5 = MN, 6 = R
6542      // H/W/Y don't get codes but don't break sequences either
6543      // Initialize lastCode to a value that won't match any real code
6544      var lastCode = '\0';
6545
6546      for (var i = 1; i < upper.length() && result.length() < 4; i++) {
6547         var c = upper.charAt(i);
6548         var code = getSoundexCode(c);
6549         if (code == '0') {
6550            // H/W/Y/vowels - don't add code, but don't update lastCode either
6551            // This allows sequences to continue across H/W/Y/vowels
6552            continue;
6553         }
6554         if (code != lastCode) {
6555            result.append(code);
6556            lastCode = code;
6557         }
6558         // If code == lastCode, skip it (consecutive same codes)
6559      }
6560
6561      // Pad with zeros if needed
6562      while (result.length() < 4) {
6563         result.append('0');
6564      }
6565
6566      return result.toString();
6567   }

6579   /**
6580    * Splits a character-delimited string into a string array.
6581    *
6582    * <p>
6583    * Does not split on escaped-delimiters (e.g. "\,");
6584    * Resulting tokens are trimmed of whitespace.
6585    *
6586    * <p>
6587    * <b>NOTE:</b>  This behavior is different than the Jakarta equivalent.
6588    * split("a,b,c",',') -&gt; {"a","b","c"}
6589    * split("a, b ,c ",',') -&gt; {"a","b","c"}
6590    * split("a,,c",',') -&gt; {"a","","c"}
6591    * split(",,",',') -&gt; {"","",""}
6592    * split("",',') -&gt; {}
6593    * split(null,',') -&gt; {}
6594    * split("a,b\,c,d", ',', false) -&gt; {"a","b\,c","d"}
6595    * split("a,b\\,c,d", ',', false) -&gt; {"a","b\","c","d"}
6596    * split("a,b\,c,d", ',', true) -&gt; {"a","b,c","d"}
6597    *
6598    * @param s The string to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6599    * @param c The character to split on.
6600    * @return The tokens, or an empty list if the string was <jk>null</jk>.
6601    */
6602   public static List<String> split(String s, char c) {
6603      return split(s, c, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
6604   }
6605
6606   /**
6607    * Same as {@link #splita(String, char)} but consumes the tokens instead of creating an array.
6608    *
6609    * @param s The string to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (no tokens are consumed).
6610    * @param c The character to split on.
6611    * @param consumer The consumer of the tokens.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> when the string is non-empty.
6612    */
6613   public static void split(String s, char c, Consumer<String> consumer) {
6614      var escapeChars = getEscapeSet(c);
6615
6616      if (isEmpty(s))
6617         return;
6618      if (s.indexOf(c) == -1) {
6619         consumer.accept(s);
6620         return;
6621      }
6622
6623      var x1 = 0;
6624      var escapeCount = 0;
6625
6626      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
6627         if (s.charAt(i) == '\\')
6628            escapeCount++;
6629         else if (s.charAt(i) == c && escapeCount % 2 == 0) {
6630            var s2 = s.substring(x1, i);
6631            var s3 = unescapeChars(s2, escapeChars);
6632            consumer.accept(s3.trim());
6633            x1 = i + 1;
6634         }
6635         if (s.charAt(i) != '\\')
6636            escapeCount = 0;
6637      }
6638      var s2 = s.substring(x1);
6639      var s3 = unescapeChars(s2, escapeChars);
6640      consumer.accept(s3.trim());
6641   }
6642
6643   /**
6644    * Same as {@link #splita(String, char, int)} but returns a {@link List}.
6645    *
6646    * @param s The string to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6647    * @param c The character to split on.
6648    * @param limit The maximum number of tokens to return.
6649    * @return The tokens, or an empty list if the string was <jk>null</jk>.
6650    */
6651   public static List<String> split(String s, char c, int limit) {
6652
6653      var escapeChars = getEscapeSet(c);
6654
6655      if (s == null)
6656         return Collections.emptyList();
6657      if (isEmpty(s))
6658         return Collections.emptyList();
6659      if (s.indexOf(c) == -1)
6660         return Collections.singletonList(s);
6661
6662      var l = new LinkedList<String>();
6663      var sArray = s.toCharArray();
6664      var x1 = 0;
6665      var escapeCount = 0;
6666      limit--;
6667      for (var i = 0; i < sArray.length && limit > 0; i++) {
6668         if (sArray[i] == '\\')
6669            escapeCount++;
6670         else if (sArray[i] == c && escapeCount % 2 == 0) {
6671            var s2 = new String(sArray, x1, i - x1);
6672            var s3 = unescapeChars(s2, escapeChars);
6673            l.add(s3.trim());
6674            limit--;
6675            x1 = i + 1;
6676         }
6677         if (sArray[i] != '\\')
6678            escapeCount = 0;
6679      }
6680      var s2 = new String(sArray, x1, sArray.length - x1);
6681      var s3 = unescapeChars(s2, escapeChars);
6682      l.add(s3.trim());
6683
6684      return l;
6685   }

6712    * Resulting tokens are trimmed of whitespace.

6716    * split("a,b,c",',') -&gt; {"a","b","c"}
6717    * split("a, b ,c ",',') -&gt; {"a","b","c"}
6718    * split("a,,c",',') -&gt; {"a","","c"}
6719    * split(",,",',') -&gt; {"","",""}
6720    * split("",',') -&gt; {}
6721    * split(null,',') -&gt; null
6722    * split("a,b\,c,d", ',', false) -&gt; {"a","b\,c","d"}
6723    * split("a,b\\,c,d", ',', false) -&gt; {"a","b\","c","d"}
6724    * split("a,b\,c,d", ',', true) -&gt; {"a","b,c","d"}
6725    *
6726    * @param s The string to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6727    * @param c The character to split on.
6728    * @return The tokens, or <jk>null</jk> if the string was null.
6729    */
6730   public static String[] splita(String s, char c) {

6753    * @param c The character to split on.

6755    */
6756   public static String[] splita(String[] s, char c) {
6757      if (s == null)

6759      var l = new LinkedList<String>();
6760      for (var ss : s) {
6761         if (ss == null || ss.indexOf(c) == -1)
6762            l.add(ss);
6763         else
6764            Collections.addAll(l, splita(ss, c));
6765      }
6766      return l.toArray(new String[l.size()]);

6769   /**
6770    * Splits a list of key-value pairs into an ordered map.
6771    *
6772    * <p>
6773    * Example:
6774    * <p class='bjava'>
6775    *    String <jv>in</jv> = <js>"foo=1;bar=2"</js>;
6776    *    Map <jv>map</jv> = StringUtils.<jsm>splitMap</jsm>(in, <js>';'</js>, <js>'='</js>, <jk>true</jk>);
6777    * </p>
6778    *
6779    * @param s The string to split.
6780    * @param trim Trim strings after parsing.
6781    * @return The parsed map, or an empty map if the string was null.
6782    */
6783   public static Map<String,String> splitMap(String s, boolean trim) {
6784
6785      if (s == null)
6786         return emptyMap();
6787      if (isEmpty(s))
6788         return emptyMap();
6789
6790      var m = new LinkedHashMap<String,String>();
6791
6792      // S1: Found start of key, looking for equals.
6793      // S2: Found equals, looking for delimiter (or end).
6794
6795      var state = S1;
6796
6797      var sArray = s.toCharArray();
6798      var x1 = 0;
6799      var escapeCount = 0;
6800      String key = null;
6801      for (var i = 0; i < sArray.length + 1; i++) {
6802         var c = i == sArray.length ? ',' : sArray[i];
6803         if (c == '\\')
6804            escapeCount++;
6805         if (escapeCount % 2 == 0) {
6806            if (state == S1) {
6807               if (c == '=') {
6808                  key = s.substring(x1, i);
6809                  if (trim)
6810                     key = trim(key);
6811                  key = unescapeChars(key, MAP_ESCAPE_SET);
6812                  state = S2;
6813                  x1 = i + 1;
6814               } else if (c == ',') {
6815                  key = s.substring(x1, i);
6816                  if (trim)
6817                     key = trim(key);
6818                  key = unescapeChars(key, MAP_ESCAPE_SET);
6819                  m.put(key, "");
6820                  state = S1;
6821                  x1 = i + 1;
6822               }
6823            } else /* state == S2 */ {
6824               if (c == ',') {
6825                  var val = s.substring(x1, i);
6826                  if (trim)
6827                     val = trim(val);
6828                  val = unescapeChars(val, MAP_ESCAPE_SET);
6829                  m.put(key, val);
6830                  key = null;
6831                  x1 = i + 1;
6832                  state = S1;
6833               }
6834            }
6835         }
6836         if (c != '\\')
6837            escapeCount = 0;
6838      }
6839
6840      return m;
6841   }

6843   /**
6844    * Splits the method arguments in the signature of a method.
6845    *
6846    * @param s The arguments to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns an empty array).
6847    * @return The split arguments, or an empty array if the input string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
6848    */
6849   public static String[] splitMethodArgs(String s) {
6850
6851      if (s == null)
6852         return new String[0];
6853      if (isEmpty(s))
6854         return new String[0];
6855      if (s.indexOf(',') == -1)
6856         return array(s);
6857
6858      var l = new LinkedList<String>();
6859      var sArray = s.toCharArray();
6860      var x1 = 0;
6861      var paramDepth = 0;
6862
6863      for (var i = 0; i < sArray.length; i++) {
6864         var c = s.charAt(i);
6865         if (c == '>')
6866            paramDepth++;
6867         else if (c == '<')
6868            paramDepth--;
6869         else if (c == ',' && paramDepth == 0) {
6870            var s2 = new String(sArray, x1, i - x1);
6871            l.add(s2.trim());
6872            x1 = i + 1;
6873         }
6874      }
6875
6876      var s2 = new String(sArray, x1, sArray.length - x1);
6877      l.add(s2.trim());
6878
6879      return l.toArray(new String[l.size()]);
6880   }

6882   /**
6883    * Splits a comma-delimited list containing "nesting constructs".
6884    *
6885    * Nesting constructs are simple embedded "{...}" comma-delimted lists.
6886    *
6887    * Example:
6888    *    "a{b,c},d" -> ["a{b,c}","d"]
6889    *
6890    * Handles escapes and trims whitespace from tokens.
6891    *
6892    * @param s The input string.
6893    * @return
6894    *    The results, or an empty list if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
6895    *    <br>An empty string results in an empty list.
6896    */
6897   public static List<String> splitNested(String s) {
6898      var escapeChars = getEscapeSet(',');
6899
6900      if (s == null)
6901         return Collections.emptyList();
6902      if (isEmpty(s))
6903         return Collections.emptyList();
6904      if (s.indexOf(',') == -1)
6905         return Collections.singletonList(trim(s));
6906
6907      var l = new LinkedList<String>();
6908
6909      var x1 = 0;
6910      var inEscape = false;
6911      var depthCount = 0;
6912
6913      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
6914         var c = s.charAt(i);
6915         if (inEscape) {
6916            if (c == '\\') {
6917               inEscape = false;
6918            }
6919         } else {
6920            if (c == '\\') {
6921               inEscape = true;
6922            } else if (c == '{') {
6923               depthCount++;
6924            } else if (c == '}') {
6925               depthCount--;
6926            } else if (c == ',' && depthCount == 0) {
6927               l.add(trim(unescapeChars(s.substring(x1, i), escapeChars)));
6928               x1 = i + 1;
6929            }
6930         }
6931      }
6932      l.add(trim(unescapeChars(s.substring(x1, s.length()), escapeChars)));
6933
6934      return l;
6935   }

6937   /**
6938    * Splits a nested comma-delimited list.
6939    *
6940    * Nesting constructs are simple embedded "{...}" comma-delimted lists.
6941    *
6942    * Example:
6943    *    "a{b,c{d,e}}" -> ["b","c{d,e}"]
6944    *
6945    * Handles escapes and trims whitespace from tokens.
6946    *
6947    * @param s The input string.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or empty (a <jk>null</jk> or empty argument throws {@link IllegalArgumentException}).
6948    * @return
6949    *    The results.
6950    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the input was <jk>null</jk> or empty.
6951    */
6952   public static List<String> splitNestedInner(String s) {
6953      req(isNotNull(s), "String was null.");
6954      req(isNotEmpty(s), "String was empty.");
6955
6956      // S1: Looking for '{'
6957      // S2: Found '{', looking for '}'
6958
6959      var start = -1;
6960      var end = -1;
6961      var state = S1;
6962
6963      var depth = 0;
6964      var inEscape = false;
6965
6966      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
6967         var c = s.charAt(i);
6968         if (inEscape) {
6969            if (c == '\\') {
6970               inEscape = false;
6971            }
6972         } else {
6973            if (c == '\\') {
6974               inEscape = true;
6975            } else if (state == S1) {
6976               if (c == '{') {
6977                  start = i + 1;
6978                  state = S2;
6979               }
6980            } else /* state == S2 */ {
6981               if (c == '{') {
6982                  depth++;
6983               } else if (depth > 0 && c == '}') {
6984                  depth--;
6985               } else if (c == '}') {
6986                  end = i;
6987                  break;
6988               }
6989            }
6990         }
6991      }
6992
6993      if (start == -1)
6994         throw iaex("Start character { not found in string:  %s", s);
6995      if (end == -1)
6996         throw iaex("End character } not found in string  %s", s);
6997      return splitNested(s.substring(start, end));
6998   }

7000   /**
7001    * Splits a space-delimited string with optionally quoted arguments.
7002    *
7003    * <p>
7004    * Examples:
7005    * <ul>
7006    *    <li><js>"foo"</js> =&gt; <c>["foo"]</c>
7007    *    <li><js>" foo "</js> =&gt; <c>["foo"]</c>
7008    *    <li><js>"foo bar baz"</js> =&gt; <c>["foo","bar","baz"]</c>
7009    *    <li><js>"foo 'bar baz'"</js> =&gt; <c>["foo","bar baz"]</c>
7010    *    <li><js>"foo \"bar baz\""</js> =&gt; <c>["foo","bar baz"]</c>
7011    *    <li><js>"foo 'bar\'baz'"</js> =&gt; <c>["foo","bar'baz"]</c>
7012    * </ul>
7013    *
7014    * @param s The input string.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns an empty array).
7015    * @return
7016    *    The results, or an empty array if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
7017    *    <br>An empty string results in an empty array.
7018    */
7019   public static String[] splitQuoted(String s) {
7020      return splitQuoted(s, false);
7021   }
7022
7023   /**
7024    * Same as {@link StringUtils#splitQuoted(String)} but allows you to optionally keep the quote characters.
7025    *
7026    * @param s The input string.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns an empty array).
7027    * @param keepQuotes If <jk>true</jk>, quote characters are kept on the tokens.
7028    * @return
7029    *    The results, or an empty array if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
7030    *    <br>An empty string results in an empty array.
7031    */
7032   @SuppressWarnings({
7033      "java:S2583" // State variables persist across loop iterations
7034   })
7035   public static String[] splitQuoted(String s, boolean keepQuotes) {
7036
7037      if (s == null)
7038         return new String[0];
7039
7040      s = s.trim();
7041
7042      if (isEmpty(s))
7043         return array();
7044
7045      if (! containsAny(s, ' ', '\t', '\'', '"'))
7046         return array(s);
7047
7048      // S1: Looking for start of token.
7049      // S2: Found ', looking for end '
7050      // S3: Found ", looking for end "
7051      // S4: Found non-whitespace, looking for end whitespace.
7052
7053      var state = S1;
7054
7055      var isInEscape = false;
7056      var needsUnescape = false;
7057      var mark = 0;
7058
7059      var l = new ArrayList<String>();
7060      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
7061         var c = s.charAt(i);
7062
7063         if (state == S1) {
7064            if (c == '\'') {
7065               state = S2;
7066               mark = keepQuotes ? i : i + 1;
7067            } else if (c == '"') {
7068               state = S3;
7069               mark = keepQuotes ? i : i + 1;
7070            } else if (c != ' ' && c != '\t') {
7071               state = S4;
7072               mark = i;
7073            }
7074         } else if (state == S2 || state == S3) {
7075            if (c == '\\') {
7076               isInEscape = ! isInEscape;
7077               if (isInEscape)
7078                  needsUnescape = ! keepQuotes;
7079            } else if (! isInEscape) {
7080               if (c == (state == S2 ? '\'' : '"')) {
7081                  var s2 = s.substring(mark, keepQuotes ? i + 1 : i);
7082                  if (needsUnescape)
7083                     s2 = unescapeChars(s2, QUOTE_ESCAPE_SET);
7084                  l.add(s2);
7085                  state = S1;
7086                  isInEscape = needsUnescape = false;
7087               }
7088            } else {
7089               isInEscape = false;
7090            }
7091         } else /* state == S4 */ {
7092            if (c == ' ' || c == '\t') {
7093               l.add(s.substring(mark, i));
7094               state = S1;
7095            }
7096         }
7097      }
7098      if (state == S4)
7099         l.add(s.substring(mark));
7100      else if (state == S2 || state == S3)
7101         throw iaex("Unmatched string quotes: %s", s);
7102      return l.toArray(new String[l.size()]);
7103   }

7105   /**
7106    * An efficient method for checking if a string starts with a character.
7107    *
7108    * @param s The string to check.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
7109    * @param c The character to check for.
7110    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the specified string is not <jk>null</jk> and starts with the specified character.
7111    */
7112   public static boolean startsWith(String s, char c) {
7113      if (isNotNull(s)) {
7114         var i = s.length();
7115         if (i > 0)
7116            return s.charAt(0) == c;
7117      }
7118      return false;
7119   }

7126    *    startsWithIgnoreCase(<js>"Hello World"</js>, <js>"hello"</js>);     <jc>// true</jc>

7165   /**
7166    * Strips invalid characters such as CTRL characters from a string meant to be encoded
7167    * as an HTTP header value.
7168    *
7169    * @param s The string to strip chars from.
7170    * @return The string with invalid characters removed.
7171    */
7172   public static String stripInvalidHttpHeaderChars(String s) {
7173
7174      if (s == null)
7175         return null;
7176
7177      var needsReplace = false;
7178      for (var i = 0; i < s.length() && ! needsReplace; i++)
7179         needsReplace |= HTTP_HEADER_CHARS.contains(s.charAt(i));
7180
7181      if (! needsReplace)

7183
7184      var sb = new StringBuilder(s.length());
7185      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {

7187         if (HTTP_HEADER_CHARS.contains(c))
7188            sb.append(c);
7189      }
7190
7191      return sb.toString();

7194   /**
7195    * Returns the substring after the first occurrence of a separator.
7196    *
7197    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
7198    * <p class='bjava'>
7199    *    substringAfter(<jk>null</jk>, <js>"."</js>);              <jc>// null</jc>
7200    *    substringAfter(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <jk>null</jk>);    <jc>// ""</jc>
7201    *    substringAfter(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <js>"."</js>);     <jc>// "world"</jc>
7202    *    substringAfter(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <js>"xyz"</js>);   <jc>// ""</jc>
7203    * </p>
7204    *
7205    * @param str The string to get a substring from.
7206    * @param separator The separator string.
7207    * @return The substring after the first occurrence of the separator, or empty string if separator not found.
7208    */
7209   public static String substringAfter(String str, String separator) {
7210      if (isEmpty(str))
7211         return str;
7212      if (separator == null)
7213         return "";
7214      var pos = str.indexOf(separator);
7215      if (pos == -1)
7216         return "";
7217      return str.substring(pos + separator.length());
7218   }

7226    *    substringBefore(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <jk>null</jk>);    <jc>// "hello.world"</jc>
7227    *    substringBefore(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <js>"."</js>);     <jc>// "hello"</jc>

7230    *

7244   /**
7245    * Returns the substring between two delimiters.
7246    *
7247    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
7248    * <p class='bjava'>
7249    *    substringBetween(<jk>null</jk>, <js>"&lt;"</js>, <js>"&gt;"</js>);              <jc>// null</jc>
7250    *    substringBetween(<js>"&lt;hello&gt;"</js>, <js>"&lt;"</js>, <js>"&gt;"</js>);   <jc>// "hello"</jc>
7251    *    substringBetween(<js>"&lt;hello&gt;"</js>, <js>"["</js>, <js>"]"</js>);         <jc>// null</jc>
7252    * </p>
7253    *
7254    * @param str The string to get a substring from.
7255    * @param open The opening delimiter.
7256    * @param close The closing delimiter.
7257    * @return The substring between the delimiters, or <jk>null</jk> if delimiters not found.
7258    */
7259   public static String substringBetween(String str, String open, String close) {
7260      if (str == null || open == null || close == null)
7261         return null;
7262      var start = str.indexOf(open);
7263      if (start == -1)
7264         return null;
7265      var end = str.indexOf(close, start + open.length());
7266      if (end == -1)
7267         return null;
7268      return str.substring(start + open.length(), end);
7269   }

7271   /**
7272    * Swaps the case of all characters in a string.
7273    *
7274    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
7275    * <p class='bjava'>
7276    *    swapCase(<js>"Hello World"</js>);   <jc>// "hELLO wORLD"</jc>
7277    *    swapCase(<js>"ABC123xyz"</js>);     <jc>// "abc123XYZ"</jc>
7278    * </p>
7279    *
7280    * @param str The string to process.
7281    * @return The string with case swapped, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
7282    */
7283   public static String swapCase(String str) {
7284      if (str == null)
7285         return null;
7286      var sb = new StringBuilder(str.length());
7287      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
7288         var c = str.charAt(i);
7289         if (LETTER_UC.contains(c))
7290            sb.append(Character.toLowerCase(c));
7291         else if (LETTER_LC.contains(c))
7292            sb.append(Character.toUpperCase(c));
7293         else
7294            sb.append(c);
7295      }
7296      return sb.toString();
7297   }

7299   /**
7300    * Converts a string to Title Case format (first letter of each word capitalized, separated by spaces).
7301    *
7302    * <p>
7303    * Handles various input formats:
7304    * <ul>
7305    *   <li>CamelCase: "helloWorld" → "Hello World"</li>
7306    *   <li>PascalCase: "HelloWorld" → "Hello World"</li>
7307    *   <li>Snake_case: "hello_world" → "Hello World"</li>
7308    *   <li>Kebab-case: "hello-world" → "Hello World"</li>
7309    * </ul>
7310    *
7311    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
7312    * <p class='bjava'>
7313    *    titleCase(<jk>null</jk>);                    <jc>// null</jc>
7314    *    titleCase(<js>""</js>);                      <jc>// ""</jc>
7315    *    titleCase(<js>"hello world"</js>);           <jc>// "Hello World"</jc>
7316    *    titleCase(<js>"helloWorld"</js>);            <jc>// "Hello World"</jc>
7317    *    titleCase(<js>"hello_world"</js>);           <jc>// "Hello World"</jc>
7318    *    titleCase(<js>"hello-world"</js>);           <jc>// "Hello World"</jc>
7319    * </p>
7320    *
7321    * @param str The string to convert.
7322    * @return The Title Case string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
7323    */
7324   public static String titleCase(String str) {
7325      if (str == null)
7326         return null;
7327      if (isEmpty(str))
7328         return str;
7329
7330      var words = splitWords(str);
7331      if (words.isEmpty())
7332         return "";
7333
7334      var result = new StringBuilder();
7335      for (var i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
7336         if (i > 0)
7337            result.append(' ');
7338         result.append(capitalize(words.get(i).toLowerCase()));
7339      }
7340
7341      return result.toString();
7342   }

7344   /**
7345    * Converts the specified object to a comma-delimited list.
7346    *
7347    * @param o The object to convert.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <jk>null</jk>).
7348    * @return The specified object as a comma-delimited list, or <jk>null</jk> if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
7349    */
7350   public static String toCdl(Object o) {
7351      if (o == null)
7352         return null;
7353      if (isArray(o)) {
7354         var sb = new StringBuilder();
7355         for (int i = 0, j = Array.getLength(o); i < j; i++) {
7356            if (i > 0)
7357               sb.append(", ");
7358            sb.append(Array.get(o, i));
7359         }
7360         return sb.toString();
7361      }
7362      if (o instanceof Collection<?> o2)
7363         return join(o2, ", ");
7364      return o.toString();
7365   }

7367   /**
7368    * Converts the specified byte into a 2 hexadecimal characters.
7369    *
7370    * @param b The number to convert to hex.
7371    * @return A <code><jk>char</jk>[2]</code> containing the specified characters.
7372    */
7373   public static String toHex(byte b) {
7374      var c = new char[2];
7375      var v = b & 0xFF;
7376      c[0] = HEX[v >>> 4];
7377      c[1] = HEX[v & 0x0F];
7378      return new String(c);

7383    *
7384    * @param bytes The bytes to convert to hexadecimal.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
7385    * @return A new string consisting of hexadecimal characters.

7388      var sb = new StringBuilder(bytes.length * 2);

7406   /**
7407    * Converts the specified number into a 2 hexadecimal characters.
7408    *
7409    * @param num The number to convert to hex.
7410    * @return A <code><jk>char</jk>[2]</code> containing the specified characters.
7411    */
7412   public static char[] toHex2(int num) {
7413      if (num < 0 || num > 255)
7414         throw new NumberFormatException("toHex2 can only be used on numbers between 0 and 255");
7415      var n = new char[2];
7416      var a = num % 16;
7417      n[1] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7418      a = (num / 16) % 16;
7419      n[0] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7420      return n;
7421   }

7423   /**
7424    * Converts the specified number into a 4 hexadecimal characters.
7425    *
7426    * @param num The number to convert to hex.
7427    * @return A <code><jk>char</jk>[4]</code> containing the specified characters.
7428    * @throws NumberFormatException If the number is negative.
7429    */
7430   public static char[] toHex4(int num) {
7431      if (num < 0)
7432         throw new NumberFormatException("toHex4 can only be used on non-negative numbers");
7433      var n = new char[4];
7434      var a = num % 16;
7435      n[3] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7436      var base = 16;
7437      for (var i = 1; i < 4; i++) {
7438         a = (num / base) % 16;
7439         base <<= 4;
7440         n[3 - i] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7441      }
7442      return n;
7443   }

7445   /**
7446    * Converts the specified number into a 8 hexadecimal characters.
7447    *

7450    * @throws NumberFormatException If the number is negative.
7451    */
7452   public static char[] toHex8(long num) {
7453      if (num < 0)
7454         throw new NumberFormatException("toHex8 can only be used on non-negative numbers");
7455      var n = new char[8];
7456      var a = num % 16;
7457      n[7] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7458      var base = 16;
7459      for (var i = 1; i < 8; i++) {
7460         a = (num / base) % 16;
7461         base <<= 4;
7462         n[7 - i] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7463      }
7464      return n;
7465   }

7501    * @return A <code><jk>char</jk>[2]</code> containing the specified characters.
7502    */
7503   public static String toReadableBytes(byte[] b) {
7504      var sb = new StringBuilder();
7505      for (var b2 : b)
7506         sb.append((b2 < ' ' || b2 > 'z') ? String.format("[%02X]", b2) : (char)b2 + "   ");
7507      sb.append("\n");
7508      for (var b2 : b)
7509         sb.append(String.format("[%02X]", b2));
7510      return sb.toString();
7511   }

7513   /**
7514    * Same as {@link #toHex(byte[])} but puts spaces between the byte strings.
7515    *
7516    * @param bytes The bytes to convert to hexadecimal.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
7517    * @return A new string consisting of hexadecimal characters.
7518    */
7519   public static String toSpacedHex(byte[] bytes) {
7520      var sb = new StringBuilder(bytes.length * 3);
7521      for (var j = 0; j < bytes.length; j++) {
7522         if (j > 0)
7523            sb.append(' ');
7524         var v = bytes[j] & 0xFF;
7525         sb.append(HEX[v >>> 4]).append(HEX[v & 0x0F]);
7526      }
7527      return sb.toString();

7602   /**

7604    *
7605    * <p>
7606    * Performs character-by-character translation. If a character is found in <c>fromChars</c>,
7607    * it is replaced with the corresponding character at the same position in <c>toChars</c>.
7608    * Characters not found in <c>fromChars</c> are left unchanged.
7609    *
7610    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
7611    * <p class='bjava'>
7612    *    transliterate(<js>"hello"</js>, <js>"aeiou"</js>, <js>"12345"</js>);
7613    *    <jc>// "h2ll4"</jc>
7614    *    transliterate(<js>"ABC"</js>, <js>"ABC"</js>, <js>"XYZ"</js>);
7615    *    <jc>// "XYZ"</jc>
7616    * </p>
7617    *
7618    * @param str The string to transliterate. Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <jk>null</jk>).
7619    * @param fromChars The source character set. Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <c>str</c> unchanged).
7620    * @param toChars The target character set. Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <c>str</c> unchanged).
7621    * @return The transliterated string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
7622    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If <c>fromChars</c> and <c>toChars</c> have different lengths.
7623    */
7624   public static String transliterate(String str, String fromChars, String toChars) {
7625      if (str == null)
7626         return null;
7627      if (fromChars == null || toChars == null || fromChars.isEmpty() || toChars.isEmpty())
7628         return str;
7629      if (fromChars.length() != toChars.length())
7630         throw iaex("fromChars and toChars must have the same length");
7631
7632      var sb = new StringBuilder(str.length());
7633      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
7634         var c = str.charAt(i);
7635         var index = fromChars.indexOf(c);
7636         if (index >= 0)
7637            sb.append(toChars.charAt(index));
7638         else
7639            sb.append(c);
7640      }
7641      return sb.toString();
7642   }

8000            sb.append(c);
8001            i++;
8002         } else {
8003            if (c == ' ') {
8004               sb.append('+');
8005               i++;
8006            } else {
8007               do {
8008                  caw.write(c);

8012                        caw.write(d);
8013                        i++;
8014                     }

8045   /**
8046    * Counts the number of words in a string.
8047    *
8048    * <p>
8049    * A word is defined as a sequence of one or more word characters (letters, digits, underscores)
8050    * separated by non-word characters.
8051    *
8052    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
8053    * <p class='bjava'>
8054    *    wordCount(<js>"Hello world"</js>);              <jc>// 2</jc>
8055    *    wordCount(<js>"The quick brown fox"</js>);      <jc>// 4</jc>
8056    *    wordCount(<js>"Hello, world! How are you?"</js>); <jc>// 5</jc>
8057    * </p>
8058    *
8059    * @param str The string to count words in. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
8060    * @return The number of words, or <c>0</c> if the string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
8061    */
8062   public static int wordCount(String str) {
8063      if (isEmpty(str))
8064         return 0;
8065
8066      var count = 0;
8067      var inWord = false;
8068
8069      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
8070         var c = str.charAt(i);
8071         if ((LETTER.contains(c) || DIGIT.contains(c)) || c == '_') {
8072            if (! inWord) {
8073               count++;
8074               inWord = true;
8075            }
8076         } else {
8077            inWord = false;
8078         }
8079      }
8080
8081      return count;
8082   }

8103      return wrap(str, wrapLength, "\n");
8104   }

8106   /**
8107    * Wraps text to a specified line length with a custom newline string.
8108    *
8109    * <p>
8110    * Wraps text by breaking at word boundaries (spaces). Words longer than the wrap length
8111    * will be broken at the wrap length. Existing newlines are preserved.
8112    *
8113    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
8114    * <p class='bjava'>
8115    *    wrap(<js>"hello world test"</js>, 10, <js>"<br>"</js>);  <jc>// "hello world<br>test"</jc>
8116    *    wrap(<jk>null</jk>, 10, <js>"\n"</js>);                  <jc>// null</jc>
8117    * </p>
8118    *
8119    * @param str The string to wrap.
8120    * @param wrapLength The maximum line length (must be &gt; 0).
8121    * @param newline The string to use as line separator.
8122    * @return The wrapped string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
8123    * @throws IllegalArgumentException if wrapLength is &lt;= 0 or newline is <jk>null</jk>.
8124    */
8125   public static String wrap(String str, int wrapLength, String newline) {
8126      if (str == null)
8127         return null;
8128      if (isEmpty(str))
8129         return str;
8130      if (wrapLength <= 0)
8131         throw iaex("wrapLength must be > 0: %s", wrapLength);
8132      if (newline == null)
8133         throw iaex("newline cannot be null");
8134
8135      var result = new StringBuilder();
8136      var lines = str.split("\r?\n", -1);  // Preserve empty lines
8137
8138      for (var lineIdx = 0; lineIdx < lines.length; lineIdx++) {
8139         var line = lines[lineIdx];
8140         if (line.isEmpty()) {
8141            if (lineIdx < lines.length - 1)
8142               result.append(newline);
8143            continue;
8144         }
8145
8146         // Split into words first, then combine words that fit
8147         var words = line.split(" +");  // Split on one or more spaces
8148         var currentLine = new StringBuilder();
8149
8150         for (var word : words) {
8151            if (word.isEmpty())
8152               continue;
8153
8154            var wordLength = word.length();
8155            var currentLength = currentLine.length();
8156
8157            if (currentLength == 0) {
8158               // First word on line
8159               // Only break single words if there are multiple words in the input
8160               // (single long words should not be broken for readability)
8161               if (wordLength > wrapLength && words.length > 1) {
8162                  // Word is too long and there are other words, break it
8163                  if (!result.isEmpty())
8164                     result.append(newline);
8165                  var wordPos = 0;
8166                  while (wordPos < wordLength) {
8167                     if (wordPos > 0)
8168                        result.append(newline);
8169                     var remaining = wordLength - wordPos;
8170                     if (remaining <= wrapLength) {
8171                        result.append(word.substring(wordPos));
8172                        break;
8173                     }
8174                     result.append(word.substring(wordPos, wordPos + wrapLength));
8175                     wordPos += wrapLength;
8176                  }
8177               } else {
8178                  currentLine.append(word);
8179               }
8180            } else {
8181               // Check if we can add this word to current line
8182               var neededLength = currentLength + 1 + wordLength;  // current + space + word
8183               // Break if it would fit exactly or exceed - prefer breaking for readability
8184               if (neededLength < wrapLength) {
8185                  // Fits with room to spare
8186                  currentLine.append(' ').append(word);
8187               } else {
8188                  // Doesn't fit or fits exactly - start new line
8189                  if (!result.isEmpty())
8190                     result.append(newline);
8191                  result.append(currentLine);
8192                  currentLine.setLength(0);
8193                  if (wordLength > wrapLength && words.length > 1) {
8194                     // Word is too long and there are other words, break it
8195                     result.append(newline);
8196                     var wordPos = 0;
8197                     while (wordPos < wordLength) {
8198                        if (wordPos > 0)
8199                           result.append(newline);
8200                        var remaining = wordLength - wordPos;
8201                        if (remaining <= wrapLength) {
8202                           result.append(word.substring(wordPos));
8203                           break;
8204                        }
8205                        result.append(word.substring(wordPos, wordPos + wrapLength));
8206                        wordPos += wrapLength;
8207                     }
8208                  } else {
8209                     currentLine.append(word);
8210                  }
8211               }
8212            }
8213         }
8214
8215         // Append any remaining line
8216         if (!currentLine.isEmpty()) {
8217            if (!result.isEmpty())
8218               result.append(newline);
8219            result.append(currentLine);
8220         }
8221      }
8222
8223      return result.toString();
8224   }

8226   /**
8227    * Helper method to estimate the number of syllables in a word.
8228    */
8229   private static int estimateSyllables(String word) {
8230
8231      var lower = word.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
8232      var count = 0;
8233      var prevWasVowel = false;
8234
8235      for (var i = 0; i < lower.length(); i++) {
8236         var c = lower.charAt(i);
8237         var isVowel = (VOWEL.contains(c) || c == 'y');
8238
8239         if (isVowel && ! prevWasVowel) {
8240            count++;
8241         }
8242         prevWasVowel = isVowel;
8243      }
8244
8245      // Handle silent 'e' at the end
8246      if (lower.endsWith("e") && count > 1) {
8247         count--;
8248      }
8249
8250      // At least one syllable
8251      return Math.max(1, count);
8252   }

8254   /**
8255    * Finds the first non-whitespace, non-comment character in a string.
8256    *
8257    * @param s The string to analyze.
8258    * @return The first real character, or <c>-1</c> if none found.
8259    */
8260   private static int firstRealCharacter(String s) {
8261      return safe(()-> {
8262         var r = new StringReader(s);
8263         var c = 0;
8264         while ((c = r.read()) != -1) {
8265            if (! isWhitespace(c)) {
8266               if (c == '/') {
8267                  skipComments(r);
8268               } else {
8269                  return c;
8270               }
8271            }
8272         }
8273         return -1;
8274      });
8275   }

8277   /**
8278    * Helper method to get Soundex code for a character.
8279    */
8280   private static char getSoundexCode(char c) {
8281      if (c == 'A' || c == 'E' || c == 'I' || c == 'O' || c == 'U' || c == 'H' || c == 'W' || c == 'Y')
8282         return '0';
8283      if (c == 'B' || c == 'F' || c == 'P' || c == 'V')
8284         return '1';
8285      if (c == 'C' || c == 'G' || c == 'J' || c == 'K' || c == 'Q' || c == 'S' || c == 'X' || c == 'Z')
8286         return '2';
8287      if (c == 'D' || c == 'T')
8288         return '3';
8289      if (c == 'L')
8290         return '4';
8291      if (c == 'M' || c == 'N')
8292         return '5';
8293      if (c == 'R')
8294         return '6';
8295      return '0'; // Non-letter characters
8296   }

8298   /**
8299    * Validates if a string is a valid IPv6 address format (without network operations).
8300    *
8301    * <p>
8302    * This method performs pure string-based validation and does not perform any DNS lookups
8303    * or network operations, making it fast and suitable for validation purposes.
8304    *
8305    * @param ip The IPv6 address string to validate.
8306    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the string is a valid IPv6 address format, <jk>false</jk> otherwise.
8307    */
8308   @SuppressWarnings({
8309      "java:S1313" // IPv6 validation intentionally compares against canonical literals like :: and ::ffff
8310   })
8311   public static boolean isValidIPv6Address(String ip) {
8312      if (ip == null || ip.isEmpty())
8313         return false;
8314
8315      // IPv6 addresses can be:
8316      // 1. Full format: 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334 (8 groups of 4 hex digits)
8317      // 2. Compressed format: 2001:db8::1 (uses :: to represent consecutive zeros)
8318      // 3. IPv4-mapped: ::ffff:192.168.1.1 (last 32 bits as IPv4)
8319      // 4. Loopback: ::1
8320      // 5. Unspecified: ::
8321
8322      // Cannot start or end with a single colon (except ::)
8323      if (ip.startsWith(":") && !ip.startsWith("::"))
8324         return false;
8325      if (ip.endsWith(":") && !ip.endsWith("::"))
8326         return false;
8327
8328      // Check for IPv4-mapped format (contains both : and .)
8329      if (ip.contains(".")) {
8330         // Must be in format ::ffff:x.x.x.x or similar
8331         var lastColon = ip.lastIndexOf(":");
8332         if (lastColon < 0)
8333            return false;
8334         var ipv4Part = ip.substring(lastColon + 1);
8335         // Validate IPv4 part
8336         var ipv4Parts = ipv4Part.split("\\.");
8337         if (ipv4Parts.length != 4)
8338            return false;
8339         for (var part : ipv4Parts) {
8340            try {
8341               var num = Integer.parseInt(part);
8342               if (num < 0 || num > 255)
8343                  return false;
8344            } catch (@SuppressWarnings("unused") NumberFormatException e) {
8345               return false;
8346            }
8347         }
8348         // Validate IPv6 part before the IPv4
8349         var ipv6Part = ip.substring(0, lastColon);
8350         // Accept empty, ::, ::ffff, ::FFFF, or : (when string starts with ::)
8351         if (ipv6Part.isEmpty() || eq(ipv6Part, "::") || eq(ipv6Part, "::ffff") || eq(ipv6Part, "::FFFF") || (eq(ipv6Part, ":") && ip.startsWith("::")))
8352            return true;
8353         // More complex validation would be needed for other IPv4-mapped formats
8354         // For now, accept common formats
8355      }
8356
8357      // Check for :: (compression) - only one allowed
8358      var doubleColonCount = 0;
8359      for (var i = 1; i < ip.length(); i++) {
8360         if (ip.charAt(i) == ':' && ip.charAt(i - 1) == ':') {
8361            doubleColonCount++;
8362            if (doubleColonCount > 1)
8363               return false; // Only one :: allowed
8364         }
8365      }
8366
8367      // Split by ::
8368      var parts = ip.split("::", -1);
8369
8370      if (parts.length == 2) {
8371         // Compressed format
8372         var leftParts = parts[0].isEmpty() ? new String[0] : parts[0].split(":");
8373         var rightParts = parts[1].isEmpty() ? new String[0] : parts[1].split(":");
8374         var totalParts = leftParts.length + rightParts.length;
8375         if (totalParts > 7)
8376            return false; // Too many groups (max 8, but :: counts as one or more)
8377      } else {
8378         // Full format (no compression)
8379         var groups = ip.split(":");
8380         if (groups.length != 8)
8381            return false;
8382      }
8383
8384      // Validate each hex group
8385      var groups = ip.split("::");
8386      for (var groupSection : groups) {
8387         if (groupSection.isEmpty())
8388            continue; // Skip empty section from ::
8389         var groupParts = groupSection.split(":");
8390         for (var group : groupParts) {
8391            if (group.length() > 4)
8392               return false; // Each group is max 4 hex digits
8393            // Validate hex digits
8394            for (var i = 0; i < group.length(); i++) {
8395               var c = group.charAt(i);
8396               if (! HEXADECIMAL_CHARS.contains(c))
8397                  return false;
8398            }
8399         }
8400      }
8401
8402      return true;
8403   }

8406   private static class Readifier {
8407      private final Class<?> type;
8408      private final Function<Object,String> bridge;
8409
8410      private <T> Readifier(Class<T> type, Function<? super T,String> converter) {
8411         this.type = type;
8412         this.bridge = o -> converter.apply(type.cast(o));
8413      }
8414
8415      Class<?> forClass() {
8416         return type;
8417      }
8418
8419      Function<Object,String> toFunction() {
8420         return bridge;
8421      }
8422   }

8424   private static <T> Readifier readifier(Class<T> type, Function<? super T,String> converter) {
8425      return new Readifier(type, converter);
8426   }

8428   private static List<Readifier> loadReadifiers() {
8429      var list = new ArrayList<Readifier>();
8430
8431      // More specific types first - order matters!
8432      list.add(readifier(Map.Entry.class, x -> readable(x.getKey()) + '=' + readable(x.getValue())));
8433      list.add(readifier(Collection.class, x -> ((Collection<?>)x).stream().map(StringUtils::readable).collect(joining(",", "[", "]"))));
8434      list.add(readifier(Map.class, x -> ((Map<?,?>)x).entrySet().stream().map(StringUtils::readable).collect(joining(",", "{", "}"))));
8435      list.add(readifier(Iterable.class, x -> readable(toList(x))));
8436      list.add(readifier(Iterator.class, x -> readable(toList(x))));
8437      list.add(readifier(Enumeration.class, x -> readable(toList(x))));
8438      list.add(readifier(Optional.class, x -> readable(((Optional<?>)x).orElse(null))));
8439      list.add(readifier(GregorianCalendar.class, x -> x.toZonedDateTime().format(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_INSTANT)));
8440      list.add(readifier(Date.class, x -> x.toInstant().toString()));
8441      list.add(readifier(InputStream.class, x -> toHex(x)));
8442      list.add(readifier(Reader.class, (Reader x) -> safe(() -> read(x))));
8443      list.add(readifier(File.class, (File x) -> safe(() -> read(x))));
8444      list.add(readifier(byte[].class, x -> toHex(x)));
8445      list.add(readifier(Enum.class, x -> ((Enum<?>)x).name()));
8446      list.add(readifier(Class.class, ClassUtils::classNameSimple));
8447      list.add(readifier(Constructor.class, x -> ConstructorInfo.of(x).getNameFull()));
8448      list.add(readifier(Method.class, x -> MethodInfo.of(x).getNameFull()));
8449      list.add(readifier(Field.class, x -> FieldInfo.of(x).toString()));
8450      list.add(readifier(Parameter.class, x -> ParameterInfo.of(x).toString()));
8451      list.add(readifier(ClassInfo.class, ClassInfo::toString));
8452      list.add(readifier(MethodInfo.class, MethodInfo::toString));
8453      list.add(readifier(ConstructorInfo.class, ConstructorInfo::toString));
8454      list.add(readifier(FieldInfo.class, FieldInfo::toString));
8455      list.add(readifier(ParameterInfo.class, ParameterInfo::toString));
8456
8457      return Collections.unmodifiableList(list);
8458   }

8460   /**
8461    * Determines the multiplier value based on the suffix character in a string.
8462    *
8463    * @param s The string to analyze for multiplier suffix.
8464    * @return The multiplier value (1 if no valid suffix found).
8465    */
8466   private static int multiplierInt(String s) {
8467      var c = isEmpty(s) ? 'z' : s.charAt(s.length() - 1);
8468      if (c == 'G')
8469         return 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
8470      if (c == 'M')
8471         return 1024 * 1024;
8472      if (c == 'K')
8473         return 1024;
8474      if (c == 'g')
8475         return 1000 * 1000 * 1000;
8476      if (c == 'm')
8477         return 1000 * 1000;
8478      if (c == 'k')
8479         return 1000;
8480      return 1;
8481   }
8482
8483   /**
8484    * Determines the long multiplier value based on the suffix character in a string.
8485    *
8486    * @param s The string to analyze for multiplier suffix.
8487    * @return The multiplier value (1 if no valid suffix found).
8488    */
8489   private static long multiplierLong(String s) {
8490      if (isEmpty(s))
8491         return 1;
8492      var c = s.charAt(s.length() - 1);
8493      if (c == 'P')
8494         return 1125899906842624L;  // 1024^5
8495      if (c == 'T')
8496         return 1099511627776L;  // 1024^4
8497      if (c == 'G')
8498         return 1073741824L;  // 1024^3
8499      if (c == 'M')
8500         return 1048576L;  // 1024^2
8501      if (c == 'K')
8502         return 1024L;
8503      if (c == 'p')
8504         return 1000000000000000L;  // 1000^5
8505      if (c == 't')
8506         return 1000000000000L;  // 1000^4
8507      if (c == 'g')
8508         return 1000000000L;  // 1000^3
8509      if (c == 'm')
8510         return 1000000L;  // 1000^2
8511      if (c == 'k')
8512         return 1000L;
8513      return 1;
8514   }
