8516   /**
8517    * Parses a unit string and converts the value to milliseconds.
8518    *
8519    * @param unit The unit string (case-insensitive, already lowercased).
8520    * @param value The numeric value.
8521    * @return The value in milliseconds, or <c>-1</c> if the unit is invalid.
8522    */
8523   private static long parseUnit(String unit, double value) {
8524      if (isEmpty(unit)) {
8525         // No unit means milliseconds
8526         return (long)value;
8527      }
8528
8529      // Check milliseconds first (before minutes) - must check exact "ms" before checking "m"
8530      if (eq(unit, "ms") || eq(unit, "millis") || eq(unit, "milliseconds"))
8531         return (long)value;
8532
8533      // Seconds
8534      if (unit.startsWith("s") && !unit.startsWith("sec"))
8535         return (long)(value * 1000);
8536      if (unit.startsWith("sec") || unit.startsWith("second"))
8537         return (long)(value * 1000);
8538
8539      // Minutes (must check after milliseconds and months)
8540      if (unit.startsWith("m") && !unit.startsWith("mo") && !unit.startsWith("mill") && !unit.startsWith("ms"))
8541         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60);
8542      if (unit.startsWith("min") || unit.startsWith("minute"))
8543         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60);
8544
8545      // Hours
8546      if (unit.startsWith("h") || unit.startsWith("hour"))
8547         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60);
8548
8549      // Days
8550      if (unit.startsWith("d") && !unit.startsWith("da"))
8551         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
8552      if (unit.startsWith("day"))
8553         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
8554
8555      // Weeks
8556      if (unit.startsWith("w") || unit.startsWith("week"))
8557         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7);
8558
8559      // Months (30 days)
8560      if (unit.startsWith("mo") || unit.startsWith("month"))
8561         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30);
8562
8563      // Years (365 days)
8564      if (unit.startsWith("y") && !unit.startsWith("yr"))
8565         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 365);
8566      if (unit.startsWith("yr") || unit.startsWith("year"))
8567         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 365);
8568
8569      // Unknown unit
8570      return -1;
8571   }

8573   /**
8574    * Skips over a single comment sequence in a StringReader.
8575    *
8576    * <p>
8577    * The reader must be positioned at the first <js>'/'</js> character of a comment.
8578    * This method will skip only the comment it's currently positioned on, not all comments in the reader.
8579    *
8580    * <p>
8581    * Supports both <js>"/* * /"</js> style block comments and <js>"//"</js> style line comments.
8582    *
8583    * @param r The StringReader positioned at the start of a comment (at the first <js>'/'</js>).  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
8584    * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs.
8585    */
8586   public static void skipComments(StringReader r) throws IOException {
8587      var c = r.read();
8588      //  "/* */" style comments
8589      if (c == '*') {
8590         c = r.read();
8591         while (c != -1) {
8592            if (c == '*') {
8593               c = r.read();
8594               if (c == '/')
8595                  return;
8596               // If not '/', continue checking from this character
8597               // Don't read again, just continue the loop
8598            } else {
8599               c = r.read();
8600            }
8601         }
8602         //  "//" style comments
8603      } else if (c == '/') {
8604         while ((c = r.read()) != -1) {
8605            if (c == '\n')
8606               return;
8607         }
8608      }
8609   }

8615    * @return An AsciiSet containing the character and backslash.
8616    */
8617   private static AsciiSet getEscapeSet(char c) {
8618      return ESCAPE_SETS.computeIfAbsent(c, key -> AsciiSet.create().chars(key, '\\').build());

8621   /**
8622    * Helper method to split a string into words.
8623    * Detects word boundaries from separators (spaces, underscores, hyphens) and case changes.
8624    *
8625    * @param str The string to split.
8626    * @return A list of words, or empty list if input is null or empty.
8627    */
8628   private static List<String> splitWords(String str) {
8629      if (str == null || isEmpty(str))
8630         return Collections.emptyList();
8631
8632      var words = new ArrayList<String>();
8633      var sb = new StringBuilder();
8634      var wasLowerCase = false;
8635      var wasUpperCase = false;
8636      var consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8637
8638      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
8639         var c = str.charAt(i);
8640         var isSeparator = (c == ' ' || c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '\t');
8641         var isUpperCase = LETTER_UC.contains(c);
8642         var isLowerCase = LETTER_LC.contains(c);
8643         var isLetter = LETTER.contains(c);
8644
8645         if (isSeparator) {
8646            if (!sb.isEmpty()) {
8647               words.add(sb.toString());
8648               sb.setLength(0);
8649            }
8650            wasLowerCase = false;
8651            wasUpperCase = false;
8652            consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8653         } else if (isLetter) {
8654            // Detect word boundary:
8655            // 1. Uppercase after lowercase (e.g., "helloWorld" → "hello", "World")
8656            // 2. Uppercase after consecutive uppercase when next is lowercase (e.g., "XMLHttp" → "XML", "Http")
8657            // 3. Lowercase after 2+ consecutive uppercase (e.g., "XMLHttp" → "XML", "Http")
8658            if (!sb.isEmpty()) {
8659               if (isUpperCase && wasLowerCase) {
8660                  // Case 1: uppercase after lowercase (e.g., "helloWorld" → "hello", "World")
8661                  words.add(sb.toString());
8662                  sb.setLength(0);
8663                  consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8664               } else if (isUpperCase && wasUpperCase && consecutiveUpperCount >= 2) {
8665                  // Case 2: uppercase after uppercase - check if this starts a new word
8666                  // Look ahead to see if next character is lowercase
8667                  // This handles "XMLHttp" where 'H' starts "Http"
8668                  // We need at least 2 consecutive uppercase letters before this one to split
8669                  if (i + 1 < str.length()) {
8670                     var nextChar = str.charAt(i + 1);
8671                     if (LETTER_LC.contains(nextChar)) {
8672                        // This uppercase starts a new word, split before it
8673                        words.add(sb.toString());
8674                        sb.setLength(0);
8675                        consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8676                     }
8677                  }
8678               } else if (isLowerCase && wasUpperCase && consecutiveUpperCount >= 2) {
8679                  // Case 3: lowercase after 2+ consecutive uppercase
8680                  // Split all but the last uppercase (e.g., "XMLH" → "XML" + "H")
8681                  var splitPoint = sb.length() - 1;
8682                  words.add(sb.substring(0, splitPoint));
8683                  sb.delete(0, splitPoint);
8684                  consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8685               }
8686            }
8687            sb.append(c);
8688            // Update state AFTER appending
8689            wasLowerCase = isLowerCase;
8690            wasUpperCase = isUpperCase;
8691            if (isUpperCase) {
8692               consecutiveUpperCount++;
8693            } else {
8694               consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8695            }
8696         } else {
8697            // Non-letter characters (digits, etc.) - treat as part of current word
8698            sb.append(c);
8699            wasLowerCase = false;
8700            wasUpperCase = false;
8701         consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8702      }
8703   }
8704
8705   if (!sb.isEmpty())
8706      words.add(sb.toString());
8707
8708      return words;
8709   }

8711   /**
8712    * Null-safe startsWith (both args null-checked).
8713    *
8714    * @param s The string to test.
8715    * @param prefix The prefix to test for.
8716    * @return <jk>true</jk> if s starts with prefix (both non-null).
8717    */
8718   public static boolean startsWith(String s, String prefix) {
8719      return s != null && prefix != null && s.startsWith(prefix);
8720   }

8722   /**
8723    * Returns the string, or blank ("") if null.
8724    *
8725    * @param value The string value.
8726    * @return The value, or "" if null.
8727    */
8728   public static String blankIfNull(String value) { return coalesce(value, ""); }

8730   /**
8731    * Creates a new {@link StringBuilder} initialized with the stringified form of the specified value.
8732    *
8733    * <p>
8734    * The value is rendered via {@link ObjectUtils#stringify(Object)} (a <jk>null</jk> value renders as
8735    * the literal string {@code "null"}). Using the stringified form avoids the
8736    * {@link StringBuilder#StringBuilder(int) StringBuilder(int capacity)} footgun that would otherwise
8737    * apply when passing a numeric value.
8738    *
8739    * @param value The initial value. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
8740    * @return A new StringBuilder containing the stringified value.
8741    */
8742   public static StringBuilder newStringBuilder(Object value) { return new StringBuilder(value == null ? "null" : stringify(value)); }
8743
8744   /**
8745    * Creates a new {@link StringBuilder} with the stringified form of each specified value appended in order.
8746    *
8747    * <p>
8748    * Each value is rendered via {@link ObjectUtils#stringify(Object)} (a <jk>null</jk> value renders as
8749    * the literal string {@code "null"}). With no arguments, an empty builder is returned.
8750    *
8751    * @param values The values to append in order. Individual values can be <jk>null</jk>.
8752    * @return A new StringBuilder containing the appended values.
8753    */
8754   public static StringBuilder newStringBuilder(Object...values) {
8755      var b = new StringBuilder();
8756      for (var v : values)
8757         b.append(stringify(v));
8758      return b;
8759   }

8761   /**
8762    * Inverse of {@link #equalsIgnoreCase(String, String)}.
8763    *
8764    * @param s1 String 1.
8765    * @param s2 String 2.
8766    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the strings are not equal ignoring case.
8767    */
8768   public static boolean notEqualsIgnoreCase(String s1, String s2) { return ! equalsIgnoreCase(s1, s2); }

8770   /**
8771    * Returns the specified string, or <jk>null</jk> if that string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
8772    *
8773    * @param value The string value to check.
8774    * @return The string value, or <jk>null</jk> if the string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
8775    */
8776   public static String nullIfEmpty(String value) {
8777      return isEmpty(value) ? null : value;
8778   }
